source.title: Traditional and Heavy-Tailed Self Regularization in Neural Network Models
source.authors: Charles H. Martin; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch size affects held-out accuracy using a MiniAlexNet batch-size sweep, with RMT measures rather than the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The cited large-batch findings are prior work, not rows. The study's own batch-size sweep and reported accuracy outcomes are extracted below.
record.test_reason: The study varies SGD batch size and measures held-out classification accuracy, directly testing the batch-size effect in V5. Its additional spectral analyses do not change that method-and-measure match. Equal epoch budgets are not explicitly established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute improved accuracy at smaller batches to stronger implicit self-regularization and propose that smaller batches capture finer-scale data correlations. These are their mechanistic interpretations; the reported sweep establishes accompanying accuracy and spectral trends.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a MiniAlexNet batch-size intervention and RMT measures to study held-out performance; does not reproduce the cited large-batch studies' methods or broader benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the reported test and training accuracy and the stable-rank and MP-soft-rank measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Stable rank and MP soft rank decrease with smaller batches while test accuracy increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this MiniAlexNet batch-size sweep, lower spectral ranks accompany higher test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Training accuracy is approximately unchanged through batch size 100 and decreases at larger batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can impair training fit as well as held-out accuracy under this MiniAlexNet recipe.

record.problems: The batch-size result is reported for one model on CIFAR10; the text gives qualitative accuracy trends without exact values or uncertainty. It does not specify a fixed epoch budget for the comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Explicitly equal epoch budgets; language models; thresholds across workloads; and recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error. The explicit-regularization experiments report spectral changes without a dropout accuracy comparison.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains no readable numerical accuracy values from Figure 4(c), so effect sizes cannot be verified. No verdict is warranted for the other versions. The study is not an original source for V5.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label evaluation.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.

Does not test language models, workload-dependent thresholds, longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, or normalization and regularization changes. The text says training was up to 100 epochs, but does not specify a fixed epoch budget for the batch-size comparisons.
Measures stable rank and MP soft rank, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or comparative ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: MiniAlexNet
rows.size_stated: FC1 matrix: 4096 × 384; FC2 matrix: 384 × 192; FC3 matrix: 192 × 10
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR10; up to 100 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch sizes ranging from 500 to 2.
rows.value: Test accuracy actually increases for extremely small b, and then it gradually decreases as b increases.
rows.note: The text reports the trend but gives no exact accuracy values.
rows.check: The qualitative test-accuracy trend is correctly recorded. Smaller tested batches provide the comparison baseline. Sections 5–6 specify training up to 100 epochs but do not establish identical stopping epochs across batch sizes.

rows.check: Training accuracy alone does not measure V5's held-out performance effect. The reported trend is correct, but its previous partial state does not describe evidence for V5. The numbers_found entry '1/1' is unsupported.

relationships.condition: MiniAlexNet on CIFAR-10, SGD with momentum, batch sizes 2–500 under the reported training recipe
relationships.reason: R1 reports decreasing test accuracy as batch size increases. This supports the batch-size penalty in this setting; identical epoch budgets are not explicitly documented.
relationships.display_finding: The reported test-accuracy decline with larger batches remains unverified, and identical epoch budgets were not documented.
